html:
A Tamil Hindu theologian and teacher, the leading figure of the Sri Vaishnava tradition. Tradition gives his life as 1017 to 1137; some scholars place him later, about 1077 to 1157.

He was born near Kanchipuram and led the great temple community at Srirangam. His philosophy is called Vishishtadvaita, "qualified non-dualism". Against the strict non-dualism of Adi Shankara, for whom the world and the self are finally illusions within one reality, Ramanuja taught that souls and matter are real, but exist as the body of one personal God, Vishnu. Loving devotion, bhakti, and surrender to God's grace are the way to liberation.

His main work is the Sri Bhashya, a commentary on the Brahma Sutras. He joined learned Sanskrit theology to the Tamil hymns of the Alvar poet saints, giving the bhakti movement a firm intellectual base. Tradition says he fled persecution by a Chola king and spent years at Melkote under the Hoysala kings. Later devotional teachers in the north, among them the line that led to Kabir's teacher Ramananda, looked back to him.
sum: A Tamil Hindu theologian and teacher, the leading figure of the Sri Vaishnava tradition. Tradition gives his life as 1017 to 1137; some scholars place him later, about 1077 to 1157.
